sources.title: Energetik
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's council-owned Energetik operates four heat networks intended to serve homes and businesses and to expand with future demand; network presence and expansion potential do not establish a connection or capacity for the sample parcel.

sources.title: Climate action
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's updated Climate Action Plan links borough decarbonisation to Local Area Energy Planning, heat pumps, retrofit and heat-network connections; borough programmes are context rather than parcel-specific energy feasibility.

sources.title: Heat Networks Strategy
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth supports heat-network development in priority strategic areas subject to affordability, reliability and coordination principles; the page contains regulatory timing statements that may be stale, so strategy direction is retained without assuming current connection obligations.

sources.title: Heat networks in London
sources.verified_claim: City Hall's March 2026 analysis distinguishes existing and proposed district heat networks and notes proposed networks may be planned or potential rather than built or operational; map presence is not parcel connection proof.

sources.title: Heat Networks Delivery Unit
sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.verified_claim: DESNZ states heat-network zoning will identify expected low-cost low-carbon areas and that future five-year zoning pipelines and limited technical/funding support are being developed; pipeline inclusion is not a parcel-level obligation or award.

sources.title: Heat network zoning
sources.verified_claim: The government collection records Energy Act powers and the January 2026 consultation response for heat-network zoning; regulations and designation processes must be distinguished from actual building connection requirements.

sources.title: London Heat Network Manual II
sources.verified_claim: The London Heat Network Manual II provides technical and commercial guidance for planners, designers and developers and explicitly complements rather than supersedes other standards; technical guidance is not evidence of parcel viability.

sources.title: Energy Planning Guidance
sources.verified_claim: GLA Energy Planning Guidance links major-development energy assessment, carbon-offset practice and Be Seen post-construction monitoring to London Plan climate policies; compliance and monitoring requirements apply to proposals, not automatically to sample parcels.
